issues.legal_issue: A registered written lease stipulation concerning the erection of buildings can fall within the exception to statutory tenant protections and remain enforceable as to buildings erected after the contract.
material_facts: The registered lease required the tenant to construct a theatre and related structures, including construction of a specified minimum quality and cost.
The lease gave the landlords an option at the end of the tenancy to purchase the buildings at a stated valuation.
The tenant constructed the theatre after the lease was made.
The landlords exercised the purchase option, but the tenant refused the offered payment.
The tenant relied on the statutory protections for tenants who construct buildings on leased land.
issues.conclusion: The lease clauses were stipulations as to the erection of buildings within the exception in the proviso to section 12 of the Madras City Tenants’ Protection Act, 1921. The landlords could enforce the purchase option, and the Act did not bar that enforcement.
issues.legal_principle: The proviso to section 12 of the Madras City Tenants’ Protection Act, 1921 exempts written, registered stipulations concerning the erection of buildings, insofar as they relate to buildings erected after the contract. The Act protects certain tenants who build on another’s land in the expectation that they can remain there, but it does not protect an expectation contrary to express contractual stipulations about building. Applying Mylapore Hindu Permanent Fund Ltd. v. K. S. Subramania Iyer, A.I.R. 1970 S.C. 1683 at 1691–92, the Court held that the relevant building and purchase clauses together fell within the proviso; N. Vajranani Naidu v. New Theatre Carnatic Talkies, [1964] 6 S.C.R. 1015, did not establish otherwise.

rule.if: tenant_protection_dispute and registered_written_building_stipulation and buildings_built_after_agreement and lease_required_substantial_construction and lease_granted_purchase_option

predicates.tenant_protection_dispute: The dispute concerns a tenant’s claim to statutory protection associated with buildings constructed on leased land.
predicates.registered_written_building_stipulation: The parties made a written, registered agreement stipulating for the erection of buildings.
predicates.buildings_built_after_agreement: The tenant erected the buildings after making the agreement.
predicates.lease_required_substantial_construction: The agreement required the tenant to construct substantial buildings or structures on the leased land.
predicates.lease_granted_purchase_option: The agreement gave the landlord an option to purchase the buildings at the end of the tenancy.

issues.definition: When a tenant-protection dispute involves buildings erected after a registered written agreement that required substantial construction and gave the landlord a purchase option, the purchase option is enforceable.

issues.legal_issue: A plaint may be amended to seek possession and mesne profits where the requested mesne profits are confined to a limited period preceding the amendment application.
material_facts: During the appeal, the plaintiffs applied to amend the plaint to seek possession of the leased sites and buildings and mesne profits for their use and occupation.
The plaintiffs confined the mesne-profits claim to the three years preceding the amendment application.
The defendant objected to the proposed mesne-profits relief.
issues.conclusion: The Court allowed the amendment, reasoning that the defendant had no just cause to object because the mesne-profits claim was limited to the three years before the application. The trial court was directed to determine the mesne profits in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: The Court permitted the proposed amendment because the claim for mesne profits was limited to the three years preceding the amendment application, leaving the defendant no just cause to complain. The judgment cites no statute or earlier case for this ruling.

predicates.civil_appeal_with_amendment_request: A party in a civil appeal applied to amend the plaint.
predicates.amendment_seeks_possession_and_occupatio: The proposed amendment sought possession of the property and compensation for its use and occupation.
predicates.compensation_claim_limited_to_recent_per: The requested compensation was confined to a limited period preceding the amendment application.

issues.definition: When a party in a civil appeal seeks to amend the plaint for possession and occupation compensation limited to a recent period, the amendment is allowed.
